facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held on 12 March 2011 in Baku.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstration in the centre of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the originally indicated location.
The applicant attended the demonstration on 12 March 2011 in Baku.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the demonstration had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the police dispersal operation.
After his arrest, the applicant was taken to three different police stations consecutively.
The administrative-offence report stated that at around 2.55 p.m. on 12 March 2011, at Fountains Square in Baku, the applicant had attempted to hold an unlawful demonstration.
The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of a police officer.
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
On 7 March 2011, prior to the assembly, the organisers of the demonstration gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA).
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed a different location for the demonstration on the outskirts of Baku — the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District.
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

At the material time, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise himself with the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 437.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision in an administrative-offence case shall be given to the individual with respect to whom the decision was adopted within three days of its adoption.

At the material time, Article 437.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision sentencing an individual to administrative detention shall be given to that individual on the day of its adoption.

A summary of other relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings, the relevant provisions concerning the organisation and holding of public assemblies, and the relevant extracts of international documents can be found in the judgment in the case of Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, paragraphs 27-42, 15 October 2015).
According to the applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents from his case file.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer while he was in police custody.

No witnesses were questioned during the court hearing before the Sabail District Court on 12 March 2011.
According to the applicant, during the re-examination of the case he was not given an opportunity to appoint a lawyer of his own choosing.
The applicant was not represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer during the second set of appeal proceedings.

The applicant pointed out a discrepancy between the time of arrest indicated in the administrative-offence report (around 2.55 p.m.) and the time indicated in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A. (around 4 p.m.).
According to the applicant, his name — the eleventh on the list in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A. — was added to the report later in different handwriting.

The Baku Court of Appeal held that the case file contained only a photocopy and not the original of the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A., and therefore it had not been possible to order its expert examination.
The Baku Court of Appeal found that the Sabail District Court had failed to examine the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A.
On 12 April 2011 the Sabail District Court re-examined the case.

Police officer M.A. testified at the re-examination hearing that the applicant had been detained for having participated in an unlawful assembly, making noise and disobeying the lawful orders of the police.

By a decision of 12 April 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention by its decision of 12 April 2011.

On 8 August 2014 Mr I. Aliyev, who represented the applicant before the Court, was arrested on charges of large-scale tax evasion, abuse of power and illegal entrepreneurship.
On 8 August 2014 Mr I. Aliyev was detained pending trial.
The circumstances relating to Mr I. Aliyev's arrest and detention are the subject of a separate application brought by him before the Court (application no. 68762/14).
On 8 August 2014 the prosecuting authorities conducted a search of Mr I. Aliyev's home.
On 9 August 2014 the prosecuting authorities conducted a search of Mr I. Aliyev's office.

During the searches of Mr I. Aliyev's home and office on 8 and 9 August 2014, the domestic authorities seized a large number of documents, including all the case files relating to the pending applications before the Court which were in Mr I. Aliyev's possession as a representative.

The file relating to the present case, which included copies of all the documents and correspondence between the Court and the parties, was seized in its entirety during the searches of 8 and 9 August 2014.
No adequate inventory of the seized files relating to the Court proceedings was made in the search and seizure records of 8 and 9 August 2014.
On an unspecified date Mr I. Aliyev lodged a complaint with the Nasimi District Court, claiming that the search of his home and office had been unlawful.
Mr I. Aliyev complained to the Nasimi District Court about the seizure of the documents and files relating to the pending court proceedings before the Court and the domestic courts.
On 12 September 2014 the Nasimi District Court dismissed Mr I. Aliyev's claim.
The Nasimi District Court held that the searches of Mr I. Aliyev's home and office had been conducted in accordance with the relevant law.
The Nasimi District Court found that the documents relating to the cases pending before the Court and the domestic courts could not be returned to the applicants at that stage of the proceedings.
Following an appeal by Mr I. Aliyev, on 23 September 2014 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 12 September 2014.

On 25 October 2014 the investigating authorities returned a number of the case files concerning the applications lodged with the Court, including the file relating to the present case, to Mr I. Aliyev's lawyer.

The investigator's decision of 25 October 2014 specified that among the documents seized on 8 and 9 August 2014 there were files concerning applications by a number of individuals and organisations lodged with the European Court of Human Rights, which had no relation to the substance of the criminal proceedings against Mr I. Aliyev.

The investigator's decision of 25 October 2014 specified that the files concerning applications lodged with the European Court of Human Rights were delivered to Mr I. Aliyev's lawyer, Mr Javad Javadov.
